name: Finland
note: Anyone must report a death to a doctor or the police without delay. Once a doctor has established death, the health-care unit or doctor reports it straight into the Population Information System, so families have no registration duty. From that register DVV discloses the death to Kela, the Tax Administration and other authorities for their statutory tasks, and to banks, insurers and credit-reference agencies on the conditions the Act sets. Separately, THL's forensic doctors review every death certificate and send them monthly to Statistics Finland.

steps.title: The death is reported to a doctor or the police
steps.who: Anyone; primarily to the doctor who treated the deceased in the last illness or the health-centre doctor where the death occurred, or to the police.
steps.summary: A death must be reported without delay. The doctor must then carry out an external examination of the body to establish death and look into its cause.

steps.title: Unexplained, violent or unexpected deaths go to a police investigation
steps.who: The doctor or other person informed of the death; the police investigate and can order a forensic post-mortem.
steps.trigger: Death not known to be due to illness, not treated by a doctor, caused by crime, accident, suicide, poisoning, occupational disease or treatment, or otherwise unexpected.
steps.summary: In these cases the police must investigate the cause of death, using a doctor where needed.

steps.title: Health-care unit or doctor reports the death to the Population Information System
steps.who: The health-care unit, THL or the doctor concerned, once a doctor has established death.
steps.summary: The report is made through a technical interface or otherwise to the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV); families have no registration duty.

steps.title: Doctor issues the burial permit once the cause is established
steps.who: The doctor, to the person who has said they will arrange the burial or cremation, or to the undertaker acting for them.
steps.summary: The body may be buried only after the cause of death has been investigated and a burial permit given; if special tests delay the cause, the permit is issued first.

steps.title: Death certificate goes to THL, whose forensic doctor reviews every certificate
steps.who: The health-care unit or doctor, to the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL); THL's forensic doctor checks each certificate.

deadline.text: without delay and at the latest three months after death was established

steps.summary: THL's forensic doctor must check every death certificate or police death report and, in unclear cases, obtain more information and correct the cause.

steps.title: THL reports a death the system has not been told of
steps.trigger: THL learns of an unreported death and no reporter is known or the reporter does not act.
steps.summary: THL itself reports the death to the population information system.

steps.title: THL sends death certificates monthly to Statistics Finland
steps.summary: Cause-of-death documents go to Statistics Finland every month; they are otherwise confidential.

steps.title: DVV issues extracts and certificates from the Population Information System
steps.who: The Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV), where the statutory conditions for disclosure are met.
steps.summary: The register records the time of death. Data may be disclosed only on the Act's conditions, and the cause-of-death documents themselves are confidential.

steps.title: Kela receives the death from the Population Information System
steps.who: DVV, to the Social Insurance Institution (Kela) and other benefit authorities.
steps.summary: Data are disclosed for court and administrative procedures and other official tasks, through technical interfaces governed by the public-sector information management act.

steps.title: The Tax Administration receives the death from the Population Information System
steps.summary: Same legal route as for Kela: disclosure for official tasks through a technical interface.

steps.title: Population data may be released for statistics and research
steps.summary: Data needed for historical and scientific research and statistics may be disclosed.

steps.title: Banks and insurers may obtain population data, including deaths
steps.trigger: Request or update service under DVV's disclosure decision.
steps.summary: Data may be disclosed to finance and insurance activities for statutory tasks, for tasks required by law or regulation, and to perform contracts with the person.

steps.title: Credit-reference and debt-collection businesses may obtain the time of death
steps.summary: The data they may obtain include the time of death or of a declaration of death.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: No number of days: the health-care unit or doctor must report to the population information system "without delay" (viipymättä).

informantDuty.note: The health-care unit, or otherwise the doctor, reports the death; anyone must tell a doctor or the police without delay.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: THL's forensic doctor checks every death certificate and police death report.

electronicRegistration.note: Reports are made through a technical interface, or otherwise to DVV.

governmentPropagation.note: Authorities receive the data for their statutory tasks, typically through technical interfaces.

certificateAccess.note: Population data are disclosed only on the Act's conditions and where needed for the purpose; cause-of-death documents are confidential.

privateSectorVerification.note: Banks, insurers, credit-reference and debt-collection businesses may obtain data, including the time of death, from the population information system.

gaps: Kela's and Verohallinto's own statutory provisions for receiving deaths were not read; the steps rest on the general disclosure rule in 661/2009, 29 §.
DVV's practical update services for private parties (and whether banks routinely subscribe) were not checked against dvv.fi guidance.
Hautaustoimilaki (457/2003) was fetched but not used: no registration-gating rule beyond the burial permit was identified.
Section numbers come from Finlex's table of contents, which carries each section's first paragraph; later paragraphs were placed by their order in the body text.
